title: SDK Plugin Hosting and Extension Authoring Playbook
author: Avery Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook documents the recommended pattern for authoring, hosting, and operating SDK-hosted extensions ("plugins") that run alongside the Redwood SDKs or in customer runtimes. It consolidates developer guidance, CI templates, telemetry requirements, rollout steps, and an operational troubleshooting checklist. The goal is to make third-party or internal extension authors shipable with predictable performance, safe failure modes, and consistent observability.

Audience

- SDK extension authors (internal & external)
- Developer Experience engineers (DX)
- Support and SRE teams responding to plugin incidents

Goals

- Provide a reproducible quickstart to build, test, and publish an SDK plugin
- Establish runtime safety boundaries and default timeouts
- Define telemetry and error-surface contracts that map to Redwood Console dashboards
- Provide an incident runbook for plugin-related performance degradations

When to use

- Authoring a plugin that extends dx-sdk behavior (middleware, token prefetchers, prompt transformers)
- Hosting extensions in a managed sandbox (dev-sandbox or customer-hosted)
- Rolling out new extension versions to customers or CI gates

Quickstart: Create and host a minimal plugin (10–15 minutes)

1) Scaffold the plugin

- CLI: dx-cli extension create --name my-rate-limiter --template js-middleware
- Creates: package.json, src/index.js, tests/, integration.yml

2) Local run loop

- Start local dev sandbox: dx-sandbox start --bindings redwood-api --env dev
- Install plugin: dx-cli extension install ./my-rate-limiter --sandbox-url http://localhost:8081

3) Smoke test (example request)

- curl -X POST http://localhost:8081/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV_KEY" -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-3b","prompt":"Hello"}'
- Expected: 200 with transformed/prefetched headers and no >250ms added latency in the median path

Architecture and hosting models

- In-process plugin: runs inside dx-sdk process (low latency, greater safety risk). Best for short sync transforms (<20ms).
- Sidecar plugin: runs as a small HTTP service alongside the SDK (recommended for richer integrations). Default contract: 1 request/response topic per SDK call.
- Remote hosted plugin: customer-hosted external service called via signed webhook. Use strict timeouts and backoff.

Default runtime contracts

- Max per-request added latency: 300ms (P95) for sidecar; 50ms for in-process transforms
- Failure mode: plugin timeouts or 5xx must be treated as non-fatal unless configured otherwise; SDK falls back to passthrough behavior
- Retries: SDK performs a single retry with exponential backoff capped at 250ms additional delay

Telemetry and observability requirements

Every plugin must emit the following spans and metrics to the telemetry-ingestor:

- Trace span: ext.<plugin_name>.request (duration, status)
- Counter: ext.<plugin_name>.invocations.total
- Counter: ext.<plugin_name>.errors.total (tag: error_class)
- Histogram: ext.<plugin_name>.latency.ms (buckets: 0-10,10-50,50-200,200-500,500+)

Mapping to Redwood Console

- Add a dashboard tile scoped to the plugin_path that surfaces P50/P95 latency, error rate, and invocation volume. Default alert thresholds:
  - Error rate > 1% sustained for 5 minutes
  - P95 latency > 500ms for 10 minutes

Sample telemetry snippet (JSON)

{"event":"ext.invocation","plugin":"my-rate-limiter","status":"ok","latency_ms":38,"trace_id":"<trace>"}

Security and failure isolation

- Plugins run with a minimum privilege model. Sidecar and remote plugins must not have access to customer tokens directly; the SDK injects short-lived extension tokens.
- Input sanitization: all plugin inputs must be validated. Reject unknown control directives explicitly.
- Secrets: use dx-sdk secret store bindings or customer KMS; do not persist raw API keys in logs.

Configuration table (required keys)

| key | type | default | description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| plugin.name | string | (none) | Unique extension identifier |
| plugin.mode | enum | "sidecar" | one of [in-process, sidecar, remote] |
| plugin.timeout_ms | integer | 300 | Request timeout applied by SDK |
| plugin.retry_policy | enum | "single" | [none, single, exponential] |
| plugin.telemetry_enabled | boolean | true | Whether telemetry is emitted to telemetry-ingestor |

(Use the YAML sample below to set these.)

Sample config (YAML)

plugin:
  name: my-rate-limiter
  mode: sidecar
  timeout_ms: 300
  retry_policy: single
  telemetry_enabled: true

CI / Testing / Release process

- Required CI checks for extensions published to the internal registry:
  1) unit tests (>=90% coverage on transform code)
  2) integration smoke test against dx-sandbox (start, install, run)
  3) linting and dependency vulnerability scan (Snyk or internal scanner)
  4) telemetry contract validation (mock telemetry-ingestor to verify metrics emitted)

- Example GitHub Actions job snippet:

name: extension-ci

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '18'
      - name: Install deps
        run: npm ci
      - name: Run unit tests
        run: npm test -- --reporter=dot
      - name: Start sandbox
        run: dx-sandbox start --ci --timeout 60 &
      - name: Integration smoke
        run: ./scripts/integration_smoke.sh

Rollout and canary strategy

1) Canary (internal): publish version to the internal registry and validate with 10 internal customers or opt-in teams for 48 hours. Monitor metrics and increase sampling.
2) Controlled release: release to 10% of active customers via feature flag in redwood-console; automatic rollback if error_rate > 0.5% for 15 minutes.
3) Full release: remove flag after 7 days of stable telemetry.

Ownership and contact points

- Extension author: primary owner for code and CI pipeline.
- DX Platform: owner for sandbox tooling and CI templates (team: eng-developer-experience). Contact: dx-platform@redwood.ai
- SRE on-call: responsible for dashboard alerts and incident escalation. Pager: #sre-oncall Slack channel.

Support and triage flow (incident runbook)

1) Detect
  - Alert: plugin_errors.total > 1% for 5m OR plugin_p95_latency > 500ms for 10m
2) Triage (SRE)
  - Run: dx-cli plugin inspect --name my-rate-limiter --since 15m
  - Check traces: filter trace-service for ext.my-rate-limiter.request spans
3) Mitigate
  - Toggle: redwood-console feature-flags disable ext.my-rate-limiter for affected customers
  - Rollback: promote previous plugin container in the registry (registry tag: my-rate-limiter:stable)
4) Resolve
  - Run postmortem template and owner-created remediation plan within 72 hours

Troubleshooting checklist

- No telemetry: verify plugin.telemetry_enabled and check local telemetry-ingestor acceptance logs
- Excess latency: check network RTT to sidecar, CPU steal on sandbox, and histogram bucketing for long tails
- Data corruption: confirm input schema version compatibility with plugin and enable schema validation in CI

Appendix A — Common extension patterns

- Prompt pre-processor: synchronous in-process hook for small deterministic transforms
- Token prefetcher: sidecar that periodically refreshes embeddings or vocabulary caches
- Safe-filter: remote plugin that applies policy checks; always run with timeout and async fallback

Appendix B — Example minimal middleware (Node.js)

// src/index.js
module.exports = function (req, res, next) {
  // simple rate limit check using token bucket attached to request.tenantId
  const tenant = req.headers['x-tenant-id'] || 'global';
  if (!rateLimiter.allow(tenant)) return res.status(429).json({error: 'rate_limited'});
  // attach debug metadata
  req.plugins = req.plugins || {}; req.plugins.rateLimiter = {allowed: true};
  next();
};

Author notes and rationale

This playbook emphasizes safety and observability over raw feature flexibility. Historically, in-process extensions caused cascading performance regressions (see postmortem: ext-inproc-cascade-2025). The sidecar-first recommendation makes plugin failures easier to isolate, and the telemetry contract ensures platform teams can detect regressions early.

Related pages and templates

- extension-ci (GitHub Actions): .github/workflows/extension-ci.yml (template attached)
- sandbox-start templates: scripts/start-sandbox.sh

If you have questions or need a review, add a pull request tagged @dx-platform and @sre-oncall.
